chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

O Allah, to You is the praise. I praise You and seek Your assistance, and You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have entered the morning upon Your covenant and Your promise, and I believe in Your promise and fulfill Your covenant to the best of my ability. And there is no power and no strength except with Allah, Alone, without partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.

I have entered the morning upon the fitrah of Islam, and the phrase of monotheism, and the religion of Ibrahim, and the religion of Muhammad. Upon that I live and die, if Allah wills. O Allah, keep me alive as long as You keep me alive with it, and cause me to die when You cause me to die upon it, and resurrect me when You resurrect me upon it, seeking Your pleasure and following Your path. To You I turn my back, and to You I delegate my affairs.

The Progeny of Muhammad are my Imams, there is no Imam for me other than them. By them I follow, and them I befriend, and by them I am guided. O Allah, make them my guardians in this world and the Hereafter, and make me a friend of their friends and an enemy of their enemies in this world and the Hereafter, and join me with the righteous, and my fathers with them.
ai.seo_question: What is the morning supplication for affirming the covenant and the Imams in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This supplication, known as Du'a al-Sahar or the Morning Adhkar, is a cornerstone of daily Shia devotional practice, emphasizing the renewal of one's covenant (Ahd) with Allah each morning. It uniquely integrates theological monotheism with the specific Shia doctrine of Imamah, explicitly invoking the Ahl al-Bayt as the primary guides and intercessors for the believer. The text reflects the scholarly emphasis on maintaining spiritual continuity from evening to morning through constant remembrance and alignment with the Fitrah of Islam.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>:

‘(You should be saying), ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! For You<sup>azwj</sup> is the Praise. I praise You<sup>azwj</sup> and seek Your<sup>azwj</sup> Assistance, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are my Lord<sup>azwj</sup> and I am Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant. I woke up in the morning upon Your<sup>azwj</sup> Covenant and Your<sup>azwj</sup> Promise, and I believe in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Promise and am loyal with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Covenant to what is my capacity. And there is neither Might nor Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Alone, there being no associate for Him<sup>azwj</sup>. And I testify that Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> is His<sup>azwj</sup> servant and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>.

I woke up in the morning upon the nature of Al-Islam, and the sincere Kalima (phrase), and the Nation of Ibrahimas, and Religion of Muhammadsaww. Upon that I live and would be dying, Allahazwj Willing. O Allahazwj! Cause me to live with what I am living with, and Cause me to die when Youazwj Cause me to die, to be upon that, and Resurrect me when Youazwj Resurrect me, to be upon that, seeking Yourazwj Pleasure with that, and seeking Yourazwj Way to Youazwj and seek my Backing, and to Youazwj I delegate my affairs.

The Progeny<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> are my Imams<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, there being no Imams<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> for me apart from them. By them<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> I follow and it is them<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> I befriend, and by them I am Guided. O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Make them as my Guardians<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> in the world and the Hereafter, and Make me a friend of their<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> friends, and an enemy of their<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> enemies in the world and the Hereafter, and Join me up with the righteous ones, and my forefathers with them’.
en.sarwar: 21. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

O Lord, all praise belongs to You. I praise You, beg assistance from You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant. This morning I am with Your covenant and promise. I believe in Your promise and I am truthful to Your covenant as much as I can. There are no means and no power without the help of Allah, alone. Who has no partner. I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.

This morning I follow the original religion of submission (Islam), and the word of sincerity, the tradition of Ibrahim and the religion of Muhammad. With this I live and will die, if Allah so wills. O Lord, grant me life, as long as You want, on this (belief) and cause me to die when You will cause me to die with this (belief), and raise me when you will with this (belief). Through this I seek Your happiness, and follow Your way. From You I beg support and to You I leave my affairs.

Ale (family of) Muhammad, are my ‘A’immah (plural of Imam) and no one else is my Imam. I follow them, it is they whom I love and their footsteps I follow. O Lord, allow them to be my guardians in this world and in the hereafter and make me love their friends and be the enemy of their enemies in this world and in the next life. Join me with the virtuous people and my anscestors with them.’”
